newsitem.title: UK: Med gasoline, naphtha weaker, gas oil firm.
newsitem.headline: Med gasoline, naphtha weaker, gas oil firm.

text.p: Refined oil products in the Mediterranean were mixed on Thursday, traders said.
Gasoline was notionally weaker again in line with falling futures prices and sagging prices in Northwest Europe. Healthy supply of low octane material was seen providing additional pressure.

Two refiners were each heard offering 30,000 tonnes of low octane material in southern France. High octane material was tighter although traders felt supply of this would improve towards the end of the month. A short strike at Lavera was failing to have an impact on Med markets, traders added.
Naphtha was weaker, under pressure from poor demand from reformers struggling under the weight of weak gasoline prices.

Gas oil was firm. Low sulphur was assessed at quotes fob hi +$3/+$5. Traders said just one player appeared to have low sulphur material for June delivery and that at least two parties were interested in buying it.
Russian material was under pressure with premiums assessed at quotes fob hi -$2.00/-$1.00. Other 0.2 percent material was seen at some 25 cents above there.

Views were mixed about high sulphur with some saying two traders were trying to push the market down as they want to load cargoes soon and sell them out of the area, while others said the market would hold.
One of the said traders sold a cargo late on Wednesday to a major with one half priced at $87 cif and the second half at mean cif Med plus 25 cents.
